name: Messenger of the Winds (Assamite Sorcery Ritual, Advanced)

system.description:
The cohesion the Assamites maintain across their far-flung territory owes much to this ritual, which carries a written message to any recipient the sorcerer knows by name, anywhere in the world, provided he has a sample of her blood to write that name with. Sorcerers stationed at Alamut, with access to the clan's Heartblood, make the greatest use of it. Rumor holds that the Tremere have somehow stolen the rite for their own use.

System: The message need not be written by the sorcerer himself, but must be inked on clean linen with a pen cut from an eagle's feather, rolled and tied with white silk cord bearing the recipient's name written in her own blood. The sorcerer then casts it into the open sky, where the wind carries it away; on a successful challenge it appears in the recipient's possession at precisely noon on her next day of slumber. The ritual fails if the message bears any other enchantment. A botch delivers the message to a random recipient connected to the intended target.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two: Saracens
